//: A thin thread of temple incense from a burner or a hanging coil that is still smouldering.

name: hanging incense coils
description: Huge cones of coiled incense hang from the rafters of the Chợ Lớn temples, each with a red paper tag bearing a family's prayer.  A coil burns for weeks; a few are still smouldering, and the air underneath is blue with sweet smoke.

name: bronze incense burner
description: A great bronze urn on three lion feet, a lư hương, filled to the brim with sand, ash and the red stubs of ten thousand joss sticks.  Some are still glowing.

name: temple altar
description: A long altar of red lacquer and gold leaf carved with dragons and phoenixes, crowded with brass candlesticks, offering plates of fruit and paper gold.  Behind it the goddess sits in her shrine, wreathed in smoke.

name: stone guardian lion
description: A granite lion with a ball under one paw and a pebble loose in its open mouth, one of a pair guarding the temple gate.  Children rattle the pebble for luck.

name: carved deity statue
description: A life-size figure of papier-mâché and wood, dark with a century of smoke, painted in fierce reds and greens: one of the generals and judges of the Jade Emperor's court.

name: stack of rice sacks
description: Woven plastic sacks of rice stacked shoulder-high on a pallet in a wholesaler's stall, each stamped with the province it came from.  Fifty kilos apiece; enough to feed a street for a month.

name: dragon fountain
description: A tiled pond in the heart of the market courtyard, a coiled ceramic dragon in the middle that once spouted water from its jaws.  Now the water is still and full of leaves, and koi drift under the scum.

name: terracotta courtyard tiles
description: Gạch tàu: square red clay tiles, worn smooth by a century of feet, with moss in the joints.

name: green glazed tile roof
description: Rows of green glazed tubular tiles, the roof of a Chinese temple, the ridge crowded with ceramic dragons, carp and tiny figures from the old operas.

name: red lacquered pillar
description: A round hardwood pillar lacquered blood-red, a gilded couplet running down its face in Chinese characters.
